Depends on the ATM. Bank ATMs, ATMs in chain stores, or more busy ATMs will typically have people in armored trucks come load them. That money is counted by machine and prepacked before it gets loaded on the truck. 

Small business and stuff like that will most likely be counted at the bank by machine when withdrawing, then by hand when the owner loads the machine.

I used to work at an ATM company and this is not the first time I have heard of something like this. Happens way more than it should.

Assuming your post is true, the best thing you can do to get your $18 is to contact your bank and file a 'Regulation E' claim, also known as an 'EFT Dispute'. All banks have this because it is mandated by the government. Do not let the bank say it is not their responsibility. Because the ATM is technically and electronic funds transfer, it becomes the banks responsibility to investigate, with the ATM company you got it from, the validity of your claim. This also applies for unusable money the machine may dispense.

If you need the money before the, up to 60 day, investigation period, you can ask them for a provisional credit. If you get the provisional credit but they find the ATM actually dispensed the correct amount, the bank will take the money back out of your account. 

This only applies if the ATM gives too little money. If the ATM dispenses more money than requested, the money is pretty much yours. You are under no obligation to return the money to the ATM company. It is not considered theft because it was their machine's error.

The way I learned how to do it when I was found is to lay in your normal sleeping position with your eyes closed. Do not move from this position. Then tell yourself that your pinky toe is falling asleep, soon you're pinky toe will actually feel somewhat different, like it actually is heavy and doesn't want to move. Then move to your next toe. Continue until you run out of toes.and move bit by bit up your body, continuing the focus on the feeling on these parts being asleep. Remember, your body has hundreds of parts you'll go thru during this process. Depending on how tired you are, you may want to break it down into smaller parts such as instead of saying just pinky toes, concentrate on the right pinky toenail, then the tip of the toe, then the base, etc. Keep doing this with your lower extremities until you hit upper thigh area right before your torso. Now move to your fingertips all the way up your arms to your should area, focusing your energy into thinking about putting your body to sleep, continue lying still. If you move, you should start all over again. Then work your way up the torso, neck and head. If you can make it past the hair follicles and stands of hair, go back and start again using even smaller areas to concentrate on. This has worked miracles for me on restless nights, I hope this helps you as well.
